claims.text: Opportunity cost is the benefit lost from the next best alternative that is given up when a choice is made.

verification.method: Authored against the 0455 syllabus scope under standard v0.2.0-draft.

claims.text: Opportunity cost is the value of the next best alternative forgone, not the value of every forgone alternative added together, and not necessarily the money paid.

verification.method: Authored against the 0455 syllabus scope under standard v0.2.0-draft.

claims.text: Opportunity cost exists because resources are scarce: since a resource cannot be used for two things at once, choosing one use sacrifices the other.

verification.method: Authored against the 0455 syllabus scope under standard v0.2.0-draft.

claims.text: A decision maker weighs the expected benefit of the option chosen against the expected benefit of the next best alternative, and the choice tends to go to the option whose benefit is larger.

verification.method: Authored against the 0455 syllabus scope under standard v0.2.0-draft.

claims.text: A choice tends to be worthwhile for the decision maker when the benefit of what is chosen exceeds the benefit of the next best alternative given up.

verification.method: Authored against the 0455 syllabus scope under standard v0.2.0-draft.

claims.text: Opportunity cost shapes the decisions of consumers, workers, producers and governments, because each faces scarce resources and competing uses for them.

verification.method: Authored against the 0455 syllabus scope under standard v0.2.0-draft.
